obligations.name: Regular-point descent
obligations.required_input: Regular analytic inverse with exact center and right inverse.

obligations.justification: For a holomorphic scalar f with nonzero derivative, the actual analytic local inverse is centered at f(z), returns z there, and satisfies the right-inverse relation on a genuine neighborhood. Composing the analytic pullback g composed with f with this inverse proves g analytic at f(z). No inverse-function hypothesis is applied at a critical point.

obligations.name: Critical-point descent and coverage
obligations.required_input: All critical points and full target neighborhood coverage.
obligations.constructed_input: Isolated derivative zeros, local nonconstancy, openness, regular punctured descent and weak removability.
obligations.justification: The derivative of a nonconstant analytic germ has isolated zeros. If it were zero on a neighborhood, the mean-value theorem on a contained connected ball would make f locally constant, contradicting the exact hypothesis. A small source neighborhood therefore has no critical points except possibly its center. Openness gives a full target neighborhood covered by that same source neighborhood. Every different target value has a regular preimage in it. Regular descent gives holomorphicity on the punctured target neighborhood; continuity at the center gives weak removable singularity. Openness itself supplies this continuity from pullback continuity, so no downstairs continuity is assumed.
